sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·朗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档关于对设计的热爱以及围绕设计的文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在我还在夜店当DJ的黑胶唱片时代，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每天晚上都要带着你最珍视的300件宝贝去工作，把DJ台变成一个充满50年历史精美文物的流动快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼带来的《重构者》吧。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Sabrina Tavernisi and this is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是萨布丽娜·塔弗尼西，这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: I'm a student.
sentences.zh: 我是一名学生。

sentences.en: Don't fail us.
sentences.zh: 别让我们失望。

sentences.en: Don't fail us.
sentences.zh: 别让我们失望。

sentences.en: Over the past month, protests over the war in Gaza have rocked college campuses across the country.
sentences.zh: 过去一个月里，针对加沙战争的抗议活动席卷了全国各地的大学校园。

sentences.en: A long-distance vision for the future.
sentences.zh: 对未来的长远愿景。

sentences.en: Now.
sentences.zh: 现在。

sentences.en: I know that there's a lot going on in the world right now and there are many places to express your views, including other places in the Coliseum.
sentences.zh: 我知道现在世界上发生了很多事情，有很多地方可以表达你的观点，包括斗兽场的其他地方。

sentences.en: But today is a day when we're celebrating our graduates.
sentences.zh: 但今天是我们庆祝毕业生毕业的日子。

sentences.en: As students graduate and go home for the summer, my daily colleagues and I talk to three of them about why they got involved, what they wanted to say,
sentences.zh: 随着学生们毕业并回家过暑假，我和《每日新闻》的同事们与其中三位聊了聊他们为何参与其中，他们想表达什么，

sentences.en: and how they ended up facing off against each other.
sentences.zh: 以及他们最终是如何走向对立面的。

sentences.en: It's Friday, May 17th.
sentences.zh: 今天是5月17日，星期五。

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: Hi, is this Mustafa?
sentences.zh: 嗨，请问是穆斯塔法吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: How are y'all doing?
sentences.zh: 你们好吗？

sentences.en: Good.
sentences.zh: 很好。

sentences.en: This is Sabrina and Lindsay is also on the line with us.
sentences.zh: 我是萨布丽娜，琳赛也在线上和我们一起。

sentences.en: Lindsay Garrison, my colleague.
sentences.zh: 琳赛·加里森，我的同事。

sentences.en: Hi, nice to talk with you.
sentences.zh: 嗨，很高兴和你交谈。

sentences.en: Nice to meet you, Lindsay.
sentences.zh: 很高兴见到你，琳赛。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你们邀请我。

sentences.en: My name is Mustafa Yao.
sentences.zh: 我叫穆斯塔法·姚。

sentences.en: I'm 20 years old and I study at the University of Texas at Austin.
sentences.zh: 我今年20岁，在德克萨斯大学奥斯汀分校读书。

sentences.en: I study civil engineering.
sentences.zh: 我学的是土木工程。

sentences.en: I'm a third year.
sentences.zh: 我大三了。

sentences.en: Mustafa, tell me where you grew up.
sentences.zh: 穆斯塔法，告诉我你是在哪里长大的。

sentences.en: Got you.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I'm from Irving, Texas.
sentences.zh: 我来自德克萨斯州的欧文市。

sentences.en: My dad's from Sherman, Texas.
sentences.zh: 我爸爸来自德克萨斯州的谢尔曼市。

sentences.en: And my mother's from Nablus, Palestine.
sentences.zh: 我妈妈来自巴勒斯坦的纳布卢斯。

sentences.en: I went to school in the United States my entire life.
sentences.zh: 我一生都在美国上学。

sentences.en: I was born in the United States, but I've always traveled back and forth from here to Palestine.
sentences.zh: 我出生在美国，但我一直往返于这里和巴勒斯坦之间。

sentences.en: It's a second home to me, but my roots are in the United States.
sentences.zh: 对我来说那是第二个家，但我的根在美国。

sentences.en: And what was it like growing up in Irving, Texas?
sentences.zh: 在德克萨斯州欧文市长大是什么感觉？

sentences.en: It was fine.
sentences.zh: 挺好的。

sentences.en: I mean, we grew up in a house.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我们在一个房子里长大。

sentences.en: We were by no means poor, but only my dad worked.
sentences.zh: 我们绝不贫穷，但只有我爸爸工作。

sentences.en: What was his job?
sentences.zh: 他是做什么工作的？

sentences.en: Truck driver, a tanker.
sentences.zh: 卡车司机，开油罐车的。

sentences.en: But we had air conditioning.
sentences.zh: 但我们有空调。

sentences.en: The bills were paid.
sentences.zh: 账单都付清了。

sentences.en: You know, I had guitars.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我有吉他。

sentences.en: My dad bought me guitars, so I was comfortable.
sentences.zh: 我爸爸给我买了吉他，所以我过得很舒适。

sentences.en: But I didn't really have a lot.
sentences.zh: 但我其实并没有很多东西。

sentences.en: I didn't know any Arabs.
sentences.zh: 我不认识任何阿拉伯人。

sentences.en: I knew very few other Arabs.
sentences.zh: 我认识的其他阿拉伯人很少。

sentences.en: My high school was mostly Hispanic and African-American.
sentences.zh: 我的高中里大部分是拉美裔和非裔美国人。

sentences.en: It wasn't, weren't a lot of white kids and no Arabs or anything like that.
sentences.zh: 没有多少白人孩子，也没有阿拉伯人什么的。

sentences.en: And your mom, did she speak Arabic with you?
sentences.zh: 那你妈妈，她跟你说阿拉伯语吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 会，会，会。

sentences.en: I speak like a broken Arabic with an accent, but yeah, we all speak Arabic.
sentences.zh: 我说的阿拉伯语不太流利，带着口音，但是的，我们都会说阿拉伯语。

sentences.en: Was it part of your identity?
sentences.zh: 这是你身份的一部分吗？

sentences.en: Was it part of how you thought of yourself?
sentences.zh: 这是你自我认知的一部分吗？

sentences.en: For sure, always.
sentences.zh: 当然，一直都是。

sentences.en: Yeah, definitely a part of my culture.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是我文化的一部分。

sentences.en: And it's unique to be able to go spend a summer in a totally different country environment.
sentences.zh: 能够去一个完全不同的国家环境度过夏天是很独特的体验。

sentences.en: You know, I always loved being Palestinian.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我一直很喜欢作为巴勒斯坦人。

sentences.en: I love my family over there.
sentences.zh: 我爱我在那边的家人。

sentences.en: I always enjoyed, always more of a community.
sentences.zh: 我一直很享受，那里更有社区感。

sentences.en: I felt a lot more tight-knit than the United States, where you just don't have that close-knit of a community as over there.
sentences.zh: 我觉得比美国紧密得多，在美国你根本没有那边那种紧密的社区。

sentences.en: Do you have a memory of what that felt like?
sentences.zh: 你对那种感觉有什么记忆吗？

sentences.en: For sure, yeah.
sentences.zh: 当然，有。

sentences.en: Just waking up in the morning, going to my grandma's house.
sentences.zh: 就是早上醒来，去我奶奶家。

sentences.en: And my grandmother, my grandfather had 13 kids.
sentences.zh: 我爷爷奶奶有13个孩子。

sentences.en: My mom was the ninth one.
sentences.zh: 我妈妈是第九个。

sentences.en: So, there's people going in and out of her house, and everyone was just around.
sentences.zh: 所以，总有人进进出出她家，大家都在周围。

sentences.en: And it would always smell like, you know, rice and vegetables, whatever dish they were making.
sentences.zh: 而且总是闻起来有，你知道，米饭和蔬菜，不管他们当时在做什么菜。

sentences.en: Lamb, gusha.
sentences.zh: 羊肉，古沙。

sentences.en: Got the TV going.
sentences.zh: 电视开着。

sentences.en: Whatever crazy show they're watching.
sentences.zh: 不管他们在看什么疯狂的节目。

sentences.en: Dramatic soap opera.
sentences.zh: 戏剧性的肥皂剧。

sentences.en: Because the city's small, it's meant for walking.
sentences.zh: 因为城市很小，适合步行。

sentences.en: So, I'd just walk around and just going around, seeing the city with my cousins, just following them around, hanging out.
sentences.zh: 所以我只是四处走走，和表兄弟们一起看城市，跟着他们到处逛，闲逛。

sentences.en: I would go outside at the start of the day, and I wouldn't come back in until I'd go to bed.
sentences.zh: 我会在一天开始时出门，直到睡觉才回来。

sentences.en: Was it beautiful?
sentences.zh: 那里美吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 美。

sentences.en: I would sit at my grandma's apartment building and look down at the city from the top of the mountain and take it in.
sentences.zh: 我会坐在奶奶公寓楼上，从山顶俯瞰这座城市，感受它。

sentences.en: And that is just a valley, two big mountains, and then everything in between.
sentences.zh: 那只是一个山谷，两座大山，中间的一切。

sentences.en: It's like a cereal bowl.
sentences.zh: 就像一个麦片碗。

sentences.en: You want to think of it like that.
sentences.zh: 如果你想那样想的话。

sentences.en: And then the stars are a lot clearer.
sentences.zh: 而且星星要清晰得多。

sentences.en: The cool wind is blowing at night.
sentences.zh: 凉爽的风在夜晚吹拂。

sentences.en: It's beautiful.
sentences.zh: 很美。

sentences.en: Sixty-some, seventy-some degrees.
sentences.zh: 六七十度的气温。

sentences.en: I'll be in a sweater.
sentences.zh: 我会穿一件毛衣。

sentences.en: Just looking down at the city, looking at the mountains, trying to notice details, trying to see where I walked that day.
sentences.zh: 俯瞰城市，看着山脉，试图注意细节，试图看看我那天走了哪里。

sentences.en: Trying to map out the path and recognizing buildings, that sort of thing.
sentences.zh: 试图规划路径，辨认建筑物，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And then the beautiful sound of the Adan.
sentences.zh: 还有那美妙的宣礼声。

sentences.en: It echoes through when you're up high.
sentences.zh: 当你在高处时，它会回荡。

sentences.en: It's got that natural reverb, that natural delay, which is always cool.
sentences.zh: 它有一种自然的混响，自然的延迟，总是很酷。

sentences.en: Breaking news now from the occupied West Bank.
sentences.zh: 现在播报来自被占领的约旦河西岸的突发新闻。

sentences.en: This has turned into one of the deadliest days in years.
sentences.zh: 这已经成为近年来最致命的日子之一。

sentences.en: Palestinian leaders say Israeli forces have killed at least nine Palestinians during an arrest raid in a flashpoint area.
sentences.zh: 巴勒斯坦领导人称，以色列军队在一次突击逮捕行动中杀害了至少九名巴勒斯坦人。

sentences.en: They protested what they say is the rising wave of violent attacks by extremist Jewish settlers.
sentences.zh: 他们抗议他们所说的极端犹太定居者日益严重的暴力袭击浪潮。

sentences.en: And Mustafa, Nablus is, of course, a city in the West Bank.
sentences.zh: 穆斯塔法，纳布卢斯当然是约旦河西岸的一座城市。

sentences.en: Was there a sense of the problems between Palestinians and Israel?
sentences.zh: 你当时对巴勒斯坦和以色列之间的问题有感觉吗？

sentences.en: What was your sense of that as a kid?
sentences.zh: 你小时候对此有什么感觉？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's kind of nature there.
sentences.zh: 是的，那就像是那里的天性。

sentences.en: Like, it goes without saying, you know, there is this enemy.
sentences.zh: 就像，不用说你也知道，存在着这个敌人。

sentences.en: I mean, I mean, that's how my family got there.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我是说，这就是我家人到那里的原因。

sentences.en: You know, my grandparents were from Yaffa, which is a part of Israel now.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我祖父母来自雅法，现在是以色列的一部分。

sentences.en: And they were forced into Nablus.
sentences.zh: 他们被迫迁往纳布卢斯。

sentences.en: They're refugees in Nablus.
sentences.zh: 他们是纳布卢斯的难民。

sentences.en: There would be conflicts or the IDF would come in and arrest somebody or something, and they would be throwing rocks and it'd be chaos.
sentences.zh: 会有冲突，或者以色列国防军进来逮捕某人什么的，他们会扔石头，场面一片混乱。

sentences.en: And I was too young to comprehend it.
sentences.zh: 我当时太小，无法理解。

sentences.en: And then I saw a raid, an IDF raid up close.
sentences.zh: 后来我近距离目睹了一次突袭，一次以色列国防军的突袭。

sentences.en: And you could go after they left, you go look at the door that they blew off with the grenade.
sentences.zh: 他们离开后你可以去看看那扇被他们用手榴弹炸掉的门。

sentences.en: And like this big metal door mangled and twisted.
sentences.zh: 那扇巨大的金属门被扭曲变形了。

sentences.en: And as obviously the IDF driving off, people throwing rocks.
sentences.zh: 显然是以色列国防军开车离开，人们在扔石头。

sentences.en: But did your cousins ever talk about it?
sentences.zh: 但你的表兄弟们谈论过这些吗？

sentences.en: Do you remember as a kid, grownups at the dinner table talking about it?
sentences.zh: 你记得小时候大人们在餐桌上谈论这些吗？

sentences.en: That's the thing is it was never like somebody was like, hey, this is what's happening.
sentences.zh: 问题是从来没有人会说，嘿，发生了什么事。

sentences.en: It was just that's just reality.
sentences.zh: 这只是现实。

sentences.en: It's like you don't remember learning that the sky is blue.
sentences.zh: 就像你不记得自己是怎么学会天空是蓝的一样。

sentences.en: You don't remember learning that airplanes exiSt.
sentences.zh: 你不记得自己是怎么学会飞机是存在的。

sentences.en: So to answer your question, no, because like I said, every single day, that's reality for them.
sentences.zh: 所以回答你的问题，不，因为就像我说的，每一天，对他们来说这就是现实。

sentences.en: Did you see Israelis?
sentences.zh: 你见过以色列人吗？

sentences.en: Was that part of your family's life there?
sentences.zh: 那是你家人在那里生活的一部分吗？

sentences.en: Well, yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的。

sentences.en: So actually, it's changed a lot.
sentences.zh: 其实，情况已经改变了很多。

sentences.en: So before you just see them through the bridge.
sentences.zh: 以前你只能隔着桥看到他们。

sentences.en: So there's Israeli soldiers at the Israeli checkpoint.
sentences.zh: 以色列检查站有以色列士兵。

sentences.en: They got their big machine guns and their fancy hats.
sentences.zh: 他们拿着大机枪，戴着漂亮的帽子。

sentences.en: But recently, when I was in high school, more and more illegal settlements in the West Bank and Israel just taking over all the highway systems and travel systems there.
sentences.zh: 但最近，我在上高中的时候，约旦河西岸出现了越来越多的非法定居点，以色列接管了那里所有的公路系统和交通系统。

sentences.en: Where you do see traveling city to city.
sentences.zh: 你会看到城市间的往来。

sentences.en: The car has a yellow license plate.
sentences.zh: 车上有黄色牌照。

sentences.en: Then it's Israeli settlers.
sentences.zh: 那就是以色列定居者。

sentences.en: Was it changing from summer to summer as you were growing up?
sentences.zh: 在你成长的过程中，情况每年夏天都在变化吗？

sentences.en: Like every summer was different?
sentences.zh: 就像每个夏天都不一样？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Every summer, more settlements.
sentences.zh: 每个夏天，定居点都在增加。

sentences.en: You know, billboards of like a young Jewish family.
sentences.zh: 你知道，广告牌上是一个年轻的犹太家庭。

sentences.en: Young man, young woman holding their young Jewish baby.
sentences.zh: 年轻的男人、年轻的女人抱着他们年幼的犹太婴儿。

sentences.en: And something in Hebrew, kind of advertising, like this is a settlement, call this number, encouraging Israelis to move there all across the highway.
sentences.zh: 还有一些希伯来语，类似于广告，说这是一个定居点，拨打这个号码，鼓励以色列人搬到那里，遍布高速公路。

sentences.en: You see that more and more.
sentences.zh: 你看到得越来越多。

sentences.en: Like, I remember having a conversation.
sentences.zh: 我记得有一次谈话。

sentences.en: My uncle was delivering maybe chlorine.
sentences.zh: 我叔叔当时可能在运送氯气。

sentences.en: I forget what he was delivering, but we drove to Jericho.
sentences.zh: 我忘了他在运什么，但我们开车去了杰里科。

sentences.en: We're seeing all the billboards and the tanks driving by us and the yellow license plates and the settlements.
sentences.zh: 我们看到所有的广告牌，坦克从我们身边开过，还有黄色牌照和定居点。

sentences.en: And I remember talking to him about what Israel's end goal is and like what in his mind and the Palestinians, like what do we want?
sentences.zh: 我记得和他谈论以色列的最终目标是什么，以及在他和巴勒斯坦人的心目中，我们想要什么？

sentences.en: Like, what's the ideal situation from us?
sentences.zh: 就像，我们理想的情况是什么？

sentences.en: Practically, practically what, what could happen?
sentences.zh: 实际上，实际上可能会发生什么？

sentences.en: He spoke of it as if I asked him what the weather was.
sentences.zh: 他谈论起来就像我问他天气如何一样。

sentences.en: He explained that the cities can't expand.
sentences.zh: 他解释说城市无法扩张。

sentences.en: So they want to, again, move us out of Palestinian land into Jordan or into Egypt and have us as refugees.
sentences.zh: 所以他们想再次把我们从巴勒斯坦土地上赶走，赶到约旦或埃及，让我们沦为难民。

sentences.en: But he talked about how most Palestinians want the West Bank and Gaza.
sentences.zh: 但他谈到大多数巴勒斯坦人想要的是约旦河西岸和加沙。

sentences.en: They want that two-state solution to not be annexed by Israel like they are now.
sentences.zh: 他们希望那种“两国方案”不要像现在这样被以色列吞并。

sentences.en: And it's scary to think about because obviously, I mean, that's the other half of my family.
sentences.zh: 想到这些真的很可怕，因为显而易见，那是我另一半家人的所在地。

sentences.en: And, you know, that's why I'm so invested in it here because it matters so much.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这就是我为什么在这里投入这么多，因为它太重要了。

sentences.en: So you go to Austin, Texas to go to University of Texas.
sentences.zh: 所以你去了德克萨斯州奥斯汀，就读于德克萨斯大学。

sentences.en: How was your experience on campus?
sentences.zh: 你在校园里的经历如何？

sentences.en: I mean, were you friends with Arab students, Arab American students?
sentences.zh: 我是说，你和阿拉伯学生、阿拉伯裔美国学生是朋友吗？

sentences.en: Definitely.
sentences.zh: 当然是。

sentences.en: Palestinians and Arabs in general.
sentences.zh: 巴勒斯坦人和一般的阿拉伯人都是。

sentences.en: I'd meet them around campus here and there.
sentences.zh: 我会偶尔在校园里遇到他们。

sentences.en: And I knew about the Palestinian solidarity community.
sentences.zh: 而且我知道巴勒斯坦团结组织。

sentences.en: I knew about Arab Student Association.
sentences.zh: 我知道阿拉伯学生协会。

sentences.en: Well, I wasn't active in it until last fall.
sentences.zh: 嗯，直到去年秋天我才积极参与其中。

sentences.en: After October 7th, there was some increased Palestinian demonization or, I guess, racism, if you want to call it.
sentences.zh: 10月7日之后，针对巴勒斯坦人的妖魔化言论有所增加，或者如果你愿意称之为种族主义的话。

sentences.en: There were a couple of things in West Campus.
sentences.zh: 西校区发生了一些事情。

sentences.en: And my God, did that stick with me and still has stuck with me in terms of just understanding how brutal and inhumane the Holocaust was.
sentences.zh: 天哪，那件事深深地印在了我的脑海里，直到现在，在理解大屠杀是多么残酷和不人道方面，它依然影响着我。

sentences.en: Well, certainly you grew up in an observant family.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你确实是在一个虔诚的家庭中长大的。

sentences.zh: 但你是在一个政治家庭中长大的吗？

sentences.zh: 比如，你的父母有没有和你谈论过以色列或巴勒斯坦的现状？

sentences.en: And like, did that ever come up?
sentences.zh: 这种话题出现过吗？

sentences.en: Definitely.
sentences.zh: 绝对有。

sentences.en: I mean, I went in 10th grade and 11th grade.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我在十年级和十一年级的时候去过。

sentences.en: I was like, all right, I need to know about this conflict more than I already do.
sentences.zh: 当时我想，好吧，我需要比现在更深入地了解这场冲突。

sentences.en: And I was like, you know, I know my narrative and I know my people's history and I would love to know their narrative.
sentences.zh: 我想，我知道我自己的叙事，也了解我民族的历史，我也很想了解他们的叙事。

sentences.en: So I read Edward Said, The Question of Palestine and Orientalism.
sentences.zh: 所以我读了爱德华·萨义德的《巴勒斯坦问题》和《东方学》。

sentences.en: I read Rashid Khalidi's 100 Years' War in Palestine.
sentences.zh: 我读了拉希德·哈利迪的《巴勒斯坦百年战争》。

sentences.en: I read Rashid Khalidi's Palestinian Identity.
sentences.zh: 我读了拉希德·哈利迪的《巴勒斯坦身份》。

sentences.en: I also read Dershowitz's book called The Case for Israel and Yossi Kline-Halevi's Letters to My Palestinian Neighbor and Daniel Gordas' Israel.
sentences.zh: 我还读了德肖维茨的《以色列辩护》，约西·克莱恩-哈勒维的《致我的巴勒斯坦邻居的信》，以及丹尼尔·戈达斯的《以色列》。

sentences.en: Kind of foundational texts on both sides of this.
sentences.zh: 算是双方的基础文本吧。

sentences.en: And I would come to the dinner table and be like, all right, like, well, what the heck happened in 1948?
sentences.zh: 我会坐在餐桌旁问，好吧，1948年到底发生了什么？

sentences.en: You know, whose fault was it that many Palestinians had to leave?
sentences.zh: 你知道，许多巴勒斯坦人不得不离开，这是谁的错？

sentences.en: And at the end of the day, like, it is definitely clear that it's complicated.
sentences.zh: 归根结底，很明显，这很复杂。

sentences.en: So I came to Colombia in search of an academically serious environment with peers from different backgrounds who, because of our different backgrounds,
sentences.zh: 所以我来到哥伦比亚大学，寻找一个学术严谨的环境，与来自不同背景的同龄人交流，因为我们的背景不同，

sentences.en: we might learn so much from each other.
sentences.zh: 我们或许能从彼此身上学到很多。

sentences.en: But what I'm feeling right now is some of these people don't believe that I have a right to be at that table.
sentences.zh: 但我现在的感觉是，有些人并不认为我有权坐在那张桌子旁。

sentences.en: I want to get to the protests and what's been happening on campus.
sentences.zh: 我想谈谈抗议活动以及校园里发生的事情。

sentences.en: But just to reel it back a little bit, what happened in the days after October 7th?
sentences.zh: 但先退一步说，10月7日之后的几天发生了什么？

sentences.en: Mourning.
sentences.zh: 哀悼。

sentences.en: Mourning.
sentences.zh: 哀悼。

sentences.en: It was a time for mourning and for being with our community.
sentences.zh: 那是哀悼和与社区共处的时间。

sentences.en: And then on October 12th, we found out that students for, by the way, Students for Justice in Palestine and Jewish Voice for Peace,
sentences.zh: 然后在10月12日，我们发现“巴勒斯坦正义学生”和“犹太和平之声”，顺便说一下，

sentences.en: the token Jews who support anti-Semitic and violent rhetoric, they were planning an all out for Palestine rally on October 12th.
sentences.zh: 那些支持反犹太和暴力言论的“象征性犹太人”，他们计划在10月12日举行一场全力支持巴勒斯坦的集会。

sentences.en: Wait a second.
sentences.zh: 等一下。

sentences.en: What the hell are you talking about?
sentences.zh: 你在说什么鬼话？

sentences.en: You're planning a rally on October 12th.
sentences.zh: 你们计划在10月12日举行集会。

sentences.en: Like, we were literally still bagging bodies in the South, Israelis, who were massacred.
sentences.zh: 当时我们甚至还在南部清理那些被屠杀的以色列人的尸体。

sentences.en: To me, that was like the most inhumane, unsensitive, really just morally reprehensible thing that I had ever seen in my entire life.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，那是我一生中见过的最不人道、最麻木不仁、简直是道德沦丧的事情。

sentences.en: And it really, really pissed me off.
sentences.zh: 这真的让我非常非常愤怒。

sentences.en: I'm the river to the sea!
sentences.zh: 我是“从河流到海洋”！

sentences.en: I'm the river to the sea!
sentences.zh: 我是“从河流到海洋”！

sentences.en: And as a Jewish community, there was a conversation.
sentences.zh: 作为犹太社区，我们进行了一次对话。

sentences.en: What do we do about this?
sentences.zh: 我们该怎么办？

sentences.en: Everyone,
sentences.zh: 大家，

sentences.en: we're going to ask everyone to gather in a circle so that we can sing together in a sign of Jewish unity and so that we can stand strong in front of the people who want to tear us down.
sentences.zh: 我们要请所有人围成一个圈，这样我们就能一起歌唱，以示犹太人的团结，这样我们就能在那些想要摧毁我们的人面前坚定地站立。

sentences.en: They'll never tear us down.
sentences.zh: 他们永远无法摧毁我们。

sentences.en: Come on.
sentences.zh: 来吧。

sentences.en: And we did 22 minutes of silence, which at that time was one second for each of the around 1,300 victiMs.
sentences.zh: 我们进行了22分钟的默哀，当时大约有1300名受害者，每人一秒钟。

sentences.en: And then got into a big circle and just sang songs of peace and unity and perseverance.
sentences.zh: 然后围成一个大圈，唱着和平、团结和坚韧的歌曲。

sentences.en: It was really a moment for community, and it was also so disheartening to see our peers celebrating October 7th.
sentences.zh: 那确实是一个属于社区的时刻，但看到我们的同龄人庆祝10月7日也令人非常沮丧。

sentences.en: That was really, you know, that was a wake-up call to the fact that we have some real probleMs.
sentences.zh: 那真的，你知道，那是一个警钟，提醒我们确实存在一些严重的问题。

sentences.en: But also, I would try and talk to people, and then, you know, sometimes the leaders would be like, you know, you're not allowed to talk to these guys with the Israeli flags.
sentences.zh: 但我也尝试与人交谈，然后，你知道，有时领导者会说，你知道，你不被允许和这些拿着以色列国旗的人说话。

sentences.en: So once in a while, I'd be able to talk to somebody, and I was lucky enough that there was one person who was actually Palestinian and, you know, friendly enough to speak with me.
sentences.zh: 所以偶尔我能和某人交谈，我很幸运，有一个人实际上是巴勒斯坦人，而且，你知道，足够友好，愿意和我交谈。

sentences.en: And then, you know, we got to talking and ended up getting coffee.
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道，我们聊了起来，最后一起去喝了咖啡。

sentences.en: We spoke a lot about narrative and the importance of narrative to history.
sentences.zh: 我们谈了很多关于叙事以及叙事对历史的重要性。

sentences.en: And I would stress the importance of the Jewish story and be open to hearing, obviously, the Palestinian side.
sentences.zh: 我会强调犹太故事的重要性，并对倾听巴勒斯坦方面的声音持开放态度。

sentences.en: When the protests on Columbia's campus started, we were already hearing, globalize the Intifada from New York to Gaza.
sentences.zh: 当哥伦比亚大学的抗议活动开始时，我们已经听到了“从纽约到加沙，全球化起义”。

sentences.en: And this movement on campus continues to scream, Intifada revolution, and there is only one solution, right?
sentences.zh: 校园里的这场运动继续高喊“起义革命，只有一个解决方案”，对吧？

sentences.en: Intifada revolution.
sentences.zh: 起义革命。

sentences.en: Now, as somebody who knows the Jewish story and the Israeli story, I know what Intifada is.
sentences.zh: 现在，作为一个了解犹太故事和以色列故事的人，我知道什么是起义（Intifada）。

sentences.en: It means violence against Jews.
sentences.zh: 这意味着针对犹太人的暴力。

sentences.en: The second Intifada happened between 2000 and 2005.
sentences.zh: 第二次起义发生在2000年到2005年之间。

sentences.en: Over a thousand Jews were killed.
sentences.zh: 超过一千名犹太人被杀。

sentences.en: Thousands were injured.
sentences.zh: 数千人受伤。

sentences.en: And it was basically a series of bus bombings, suicide bombings, stabbings, shootings, perpetrated, perpetuated by Palestinian terrorists.
sentences.zh: 这基本上是一系列由巴勒斯坦恐怖分子实施的公共汽车爆炸、自杀式炸弹袭击、刺杀和枪击事件。

sentences.en: So that's what I hear when I hear Intifada.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是我听到“起义”时所想到的。

sentences.en: It is a call for violence against Jews everywhere, very, very simply.
sentences.zh: 非常非常简单地说，这是对各地犹太人实施暴力的呼吁。

sentences.en: So I raised that concern.
sentences.zh: 所以我提出了这个担忧。

sentences.en: And I said, please shut it down because this is a threat against Jews and it's going to normalize violence against Jews.
sentences.zh: 我说，请停止这种行为，因为这是对犹太人的威胁，它将使针对犹太人的暴力正常化。

sentences.en: And I was told, no, the Arabic root of Intifada is nafada, which means shaking things up.
sentences.zh: 有人告诉我，不，起义的阿拉伯语词根是“nafada”，意思是“动摇”。

sentences.en: And I said, well, you can't use etymological roots to reverse what the meaning has become.
sentences.zh: 我说，好吧，你不能用词源学词根来扭转它已经形成的含义。

sentences.en: And I was told, well, we're not calling for violence.
sentences.zh: 有人告诉我，好吧，我们不是在呼吁暴力。

sentences.en: And I would say, well, what are you calling for?
sentences.zh: 我会说，好吧，那你们在呼吁什么？

sentences.en: And there was never a concrete answer.
sentences.zh: 从来没有一个具体的答案。

sentences.en: We've had this conversation probably 10 times over lunch, in passing.
sentences.zh: 我们可能在午餐时或路过时进行过10次这样的对话。

sentences.en: We're not going to agree.
sentences.zh: 我们不会达成一致。

sentences.en: It is a call for violence against Jews.
sentences.zh: 这就是对犹太人实施暴力的呼吁。

sentences.en: There is no way that any other minority could get his claims of discrimination denied by the use of an etymological root.
sentences.zh: 没有任何其他少数群体会因为使用词源学词根而被否认其遭受歧视的诉求。

sentences.en: Everyone who has to go through DEI training is taught that a microaggression is something that you say, but you didn't mean to be racist, but maybe might come off as offensive.
sentences.zh: 每个必须参加多元化、公平与包容（DEI）培训的人都被教导，微冒犯是你说了什么，但你本意并非种族歧视，但可能听起来具有冒犯性。

sentences.en: And we're taught that the impact of your words matters more than your intent when you say it.
sentences.zh: 我们被教导，当你说话时，言语的影响比意图更重要。

sentences.en: Now, I'm saying, well, here's the impact of your words on me.
sentences.zh: 现在，我说，好吧，这是你的言语对我产生的影响。

sentences.en: Here's how I experience them as a Jew, as a minority.
sentences.zh: 这是我作为一个犹太人、一个少数群体成员的亲身感受。

sentences.en: And I'm being told, no, no, no, the intent of the speaker matters more than the impact on you.
sentences.zh: 但我被告知，不，不，不，说话者的意图比对你产生的影响更重要。

sentences.en: What kind of double standard is that?
sentences.zh: 这是什么样的双重标准？

sentences.en: You mentioned earlier this phrase, token Jew.
sentences.zh: 你之前提到了“象征性犹太人”这个词。

sentences.en: Who are the token Jews?
sentences.zh: 谁是象征性犹太人？

sentences.en: To me, I think it's really sad.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，我觉得这真的很可悲。

sentences.en: There are some Jewish people who identify, I guess, as Jewish, but reject the existence of the state of Israel.
sentences.zh: 有些犹太人认同自己是犹太人，但拒绝承认以色列国的存在。

sentences.en: And what's happening is that they're saying, oh, you know, I'm Jewish and I'm anti-ZioniSt.
sentences.zh: 发生的情况是，他们说，哦，你知道，我是犹太人，我是反犹太复国主义者。

sentences.en: So therefore, anti-Zionism is not anti-Semitism or therefore this movement can't be anti-Semitic because I'm a part of it.
sentences.zh: 所以反犹太复国主义不是反犹太主义，或者说这场运动不可能是反犹太主义的，因为我是其中的一员。

sentences.en: That is textbook tokenization.
sentences.zh: 这就是教科书式的象征化。

sentences.en: And who are they?
sentences.zh: 他们是谁？

sentences.en: I don't know who they are.
sentences.zh: 我不知道他们是谁。

sentences.en: I don't know who they are, but I do know that they do not know the Jewish story.
sentences.zh: 我不知道他们是谁，但我确实知道他们不了解犹太人的故事。

sentences.en: They just don't know it.
sentences.zh: 他们就是不了解。

sentences.en: They are signing statements and leading protests that are celebrating the murder of Israelis and of Jews.
sentences.zh: 他们签署声明并领导抗议活动，庆祝对以色列人和犹太人的谋杀。

sentences.en: How in good conscience as a Jew could you possibly do that?
sentences.zh: 作为一个犹太人，你怎么可能凭良心做这种事？

sentences.en: Have you ever been called that token Jew?
sentences.zh: 你有没有被叫过“象征性犹太人”？

sentences.en: Oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: I have been called a self-hating Jew.
sentences.zh: 我被叫过“自我仇恨的犹太人”。

sentences.en: I've been told I want the extermination of Jewish people.
sentences.zh: 我被告知我想要灭绝犹太人。

sentences.en: I have not been directly called a token Jew.
sentences.zh: 我没有被直接叫过“象征性犹太人”。

sentences.en: But I have definitely seen things online that insinuate that myself and other Jewish people in this movement are.
sentences.zh: 但我确实在网上看到过一些暗示，说我和这场运动中的其他犹太人是这样的人。

sentences.en: And it hurts.
sentences.zh: 这很伤人。

sentences.en: But I, well, I know it's not true.
sentences.zh: 但我，好吧，我知道这不是真的。

sentences.en: I know that it is not an accurate portrayal of me or my feelings, but that it is an accurate portrayal of other people's fear and desire for safety.
sentences.zh: 我知道这对我或我的感受的描述是不准确的，但这准确地反映了其他人对安全感的恐惧和渴望。

sentences.en: I also want my people to be safe, but my desire for safety is not built on the idea that it has to come to someone else's expense.
sentences.zh: 我也希望我的人民安全，但我的安全愿望并不是建立在必须以牺牲他人为代价的基础上。

sentences.en: My name is Jasmine Jolly.
sentences.zh: 我叫贾斯敏·乔利。
我25岁。

sentences.en: I'm a student at Cal Poly Humboldt.
sentences.zh: 我是加州理工洪堡分校的学生。

sentences.en: I'm a student of the Child Development Department.
sentences.zh: 我是儿童发展系的学生。

sentences.en: And I am at home in Arcata, California.
sentences.zh: 我现在在加利福尼亚州阿卡塔的家中。

sentences.en: I grew up in Sonoma County.
sentences.zh: 我在索诺马县长大。

sentences.en: I'm of Ashkenazi descent on my mom's side.
sentences.zh: 我母亲那边是德系犹太人后裔。

sentences.en: My dad's a high school teacher.
sentences.zh: 我父亲是一名高中老师。

sentences.en: And my mom ran a daycare for years.
sentences.zh: 我母亲经营了一家托儿所多年。

sentences.en: And my parents were both activists.
sentences.zh: 我的父母都是活动家。

sentences.en: They took us to anti-war protests.
sentences.zh: 他们带我们去参加反战抗议活动。

sentences.en: Like when Bush attacked Iraq, they had us at protests.
sentences.zh: 比如布什袭击伊拉克时，他们带我们去参加抗议。

sentences.en: And my mom made us all shirts.
sentences.zh: 我妈妈给我们每个人都做了衬衫。

sentences.en: Like I think mine said war is bad for toddlers.
sentences.zh: 我想我的那件写着“战争对幼儿有害”。

sentences.en: My sister said war is bad for babies.
sentences.zh: 我姐姐的那件写着“战争对婴儿有害”。

sentences.en: Hers said war is bad for moMs.
sentences.zh: 她的那件写着“战争对妈妈有害”。

sentences.en: My dad said war is bad for dads.
sentences.zh: 我爸爸的那件写着“战争对爸爸有害”。

sentences.en: And what about your faith?
sentences.zh: 那你的信仰呢？

sentences.en: Did they practice Judaism?
sentences.zh: 他们实践犹太教吗？

sentences.en: Were your parents more culturally Jewish?
sentences.zh: 你的父母是更偏向文化上的犹太人吗？

sentences.en: My dad was raised Catholic, but I was raised really proudly like culturally Jewish.
sentences.zh: 我父亲是天主教徒，但我是在一种非常自豪的文化犹太氛围中长大的。

sentences.en: So we always had really big like family seders, big Hanukkah parties.
sentences.zh: 所以我们总是举行非常盛大的家庭逾越节家宴，大型光明节派对。

sentences.en: We celebrated Rosh Hashanah together.
sentences.zh: 我们一起庆祝犹太新年。

sentences.en: I'm really openly Jewish.
sentences.zh: 我是一个非常公开的犹太人。

sentences.en: Jewish and I talk about it a lot.
sentences.zh: 我和犹太人谈论过很多次这个问题。

sentences.en: I talk about the values through like my understanding of Jewish tradition and just like historically
sentences.zh: 我通过自己对犹太传统的理解，以及从历史的角度，来谈论这些价值观。

sentences.en: for me, holding on to that title of Jewish and being able to pass it on to my children one day is really, really important.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，保持犹太人的身份，并有朝一日能将其传给我的孩子，真的非常、非常重要。

sentences.en: So yeah, like I'm raising Jewish babies one day for sure.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我以后肯定会抚养犹太后代。

sentences.en: But I have been, I've been in a lot of spaces where I didn't feel Jewish enough.
sentences.zh: 但我曾多次身处一些让我感到自己“不够犹太”的环境中。

sentences.en: And I've also been told a lot throughout my life that I don't look Jewish.
sentences.zh: 而且我一生中也多次被告知，我看起来不像犹太人。

sentences.en: I look like the Irish, English, Scottish side of my family.
sentences.zh: 我看起来更像我家族中爱尔兰、英国和苏格兰血统的那一边。

sentences.en: So yeah, like I don't in a lot of ways fit Jewish stereotypes.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，在很多方面我并不符合犹太人的刻板印象。

sentences.en: And I've never been targeted because of it.
sentences.zh: 我也从未因此成为攻击目标。

sentences.en: Um, and that at least is like, I'm sure partially because of how I look.
sentences.zh: 嗯，至少这在一定程度上是因为我的长相，我敢肯定。

sentences.en: And then two, three years ago, I had been giving a lot of consideration to the idea of birthright.
sentences.zh: 两三年前，我开始认真考虑“出生权之旅”（Birthright trip）这个概念。

sentences.en: Birthright trip is a free trip that anyone who can prove Jewish ancestry is given to Israel.
sentences.zh: “出生权之旅”是一项免费旅行，任何能证明有犹太血统的人都可以去以色列。

sentences.en: It's seen as a birthright of Jewish people.
sentences.zh: 它被视为犹太人的出生权利。

sentences.en: And then in my mid late teenage years, I had read about people walking off of their birthright trip in proteSt.
sentences.zh: 在我十几岁到二十岁出头的时候，我读到过有人在“出生权之旅”中途抗议离团的事。

sentences.en: And that sort of sparked like a bit of a deeper dive beyond the honestly, very little that I knew about the country previously.
sentences.zh: 这引发了我更深层次的探索，超出了我之前对那个国家极其有限的了解。

sentences.en: Um, and I started reading about that and I started reading about settler violence in the
sentences.zh: 嗯，我开始阅读相关资料，也开始阅读关于西岸地区定居者暴力行为的内容。

sentences.en: West Bank.
sentences.zh: 西岸。

sentences.en: And I looked at like historical maps and historical treaties and I was like, there's things here
sentences.zh: 我查看了历史地图和历史条约，我当时想，这里有些事情是我之前没被告知的，没人告诉过我。

sentences.en: that I wasn't like told that people didn't tell me, um, like what, like about settler violence and this like pretty continuous push from Israeli people onto Palestinian land and
sentences.zh: 比如关于定居者的暴力，以及以色列人对巴勒斯坦土地持续的蚕食，

sentences.en: then expulsion of Palestinians from their land.
sentences.zh: 还有将巴勒斯坦人从他们的土地上驱逐出去。

sentences.en: But that was a really big turning point for me.
sentences.zh: 那对我来说是一个非常重大的转折点。

sentences.en: So you never went on the birthright trip?
sentences.zh: 所以你从来没有参加过“出生权之旅”？

sentences.en: No, and I won't.
sentences.zh: 没有，而且我也不会去。

sentences.en: And then mid October, right around that time, there were the campus dialogues on race.
sentences.zh: 十月中旬，就在那个时候，校园里举行了关于种族的对话活动。

sentences.en: And for a class, we were assigned to go to two of these and to write about our experience there.
sentences.zh: 作为课程作业，我们被要求参加其中两场，并写下我们的经历。

sentences.en: So one I went to was given by a Palestinian student on, I think they called it like countries, like resistance, embroidery.
sentences.zh: 我参加的第一场是由一位巴勒斯坦学生主讲的，我想他们称之为关于国家、抵抗和刺绣之类的东西。

sentences.en: And at that point I was watching Israel's retaliation.
sentences.zh: 当时我正在关注以色列的报复行动。

sentences.en: Now more than 12,700 Palestinians have been killed.
sentences.zh: 现在已有超过12700名巴勒斯坦人丧生。

sentences.en: I watched the numbers of the dead go up and I watched family lines being wiped out, people being pushed out of their homes.
sentences.zh: 我看着死亡人数不断攀升，看着一个个家族血脉被抹去，人们被赶出家园。

sentences.en: Families are burying their dead en masse.
sentences.zh: 许多家庭正在集体埋葬他们的死者。

sentences.en: I've seen hundreds and hundreds of images of dead children and dead families and bodies and mass graves.
sentences.zh: 我看到了成百上千张死去的孩子、死去的家庭、尸体和乱葬岗的照片。

sentences.en: Gaza becoming a graveyard for children, the UN chief says.
sentences.zh: 联合国秘书长说，加沙正在变成儿童的坟场。

sentences.en: And all I could see in that was this parallel to how my family was treated in Eastern Europe.
sentences.zh: 我在其中看到的，全是我家族在东欧所受待遇的缩影。

sentences.en: And that was when the severity sunk in.
sentences.zh: 就在那时，我深刻感受到了事态的严重性。

sentences.en: I come from a people who are historically expelled.
sentences.zh: 我来自一个历史上一直被驱逐的民族。

sentences.en: And I felt like I was watching Israel do what was done to my family.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我正在看着以色列做着当年对我家族所做的事情。

sentences.en: And that was, that was the end of any way I could support that country for me.
sentences.zh: 对我而言，那是我支持那个国家的底线。

sentences.en: I felt like I was watching them enact vengeance out of fear.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我正在看着他们出于恐惧而实施报复。

sentences.en: And I know exactly where that fear of like exile and extermination comes from in Jewish people,
sentences.zh: 我非常清楚犹太人对流亡和灭绝的恐惧从何而来，

sentences.en: because I feel it for my family when they had to leave Eastern Europe or for the few who went to Western Europe instead of the U.S.
sentences.zh: 因为当我想到我的家人不得不离开东欧，或者那些没有去美国而是去了西欧的少数人，

sentences.en: when they had to leave France and when they died.
sentences.zh: 当他们不得不离开法国并最终死去时，我能感受到那种恐惧。

sentences.en: And I, the lesson I learned, I feel like, from my history is that I have a voice that is powerful.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我从历史中学到的教训是，我拥有一个强大的声音。

sentences.en: I feel like my Jewish family especially teaches me to ask questions.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我的犹太家庭特别教会了我去提出质疑。

sentences.en: And that is what I am trying to do.
sentences.zh: 而这正是我正在努力做的事情。

sentences.en: So I thought that if there was any way that my voice could influence an end to violence, I would try to make it loud.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，如果我的声音有任何可能影响暴力终结，我会努力让它变得响亮。

sentences.en: So we had a couple of vigils for people who have died in Gaza, where we read testimonies of their stories or some of their words.
sentences.zh: 我们为在加沙死去的人举行了几次守夜活动，我们朗读了他们的故事或他们留下的一些话。

sentences.en: That was when I got more involved with Humboldt for Palestine up here.
sentences.zh: 那时我开始更多地参与到这里的“洪堡支持巴勒斯坦”（Humboldt for Palestine）活动中。

sentences.en: And eventually we shifted to being at the Eureka Courthouse on Fridays.
sentences.zh: 最终，我们改为每周五在尤里卡法院前集会。

sentences.en: And we have been there every Friday ever since.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，我们每个周五都在那里。

sentences.en: And what was your sign that you made?
sentences.zh: 你做的标语牌上写了什么？

sentences.en: Mine said in honor of my Jewish ancestors, I stand with Palestine.
sentences.zh: 我的写着：为了纪念我的犹太祖先，我与巴勒斯坦站在一起。

sentences.en: Jasmine, during these protests, I wanted to ask you if you ever felt hostility toward you because of your Jewishness.
sentences.zh: 茉莉，在这些抗议活动中，我想问你是否因为你的犹太身份而感到过敌意？

sentences.en: No, nothing that has like ever made me feel excluded.
sentences.zh: 没有，没有任何事情让我感到被排斥。

sentences.en: I'm sure you've seen some of these comparisons of like Nazis and IDFs or people compare Netanyahu to Hitler.
sentences.zh: 我相信你一定见过一些将纳粹与以色列国防军（IDF）进行比较，或者将内塔尼亚胡与希特勒进行比较的言论。

sentences.en: And once we had a person show up to one of our regular protests with an Israeli flag, but instead of the Star of David, it had a swastika on it.
sentences.zh: 有一次，一个人带着一面以色列国旗出现在我们平时的抗议活动中，但旗帜上大卫之星的位置被换成了一个纳粹万字旗。

sentences.en: And that I was immediately uncomfortable with, I will not stand with a swastika.
sentences.zh: 那让我立刻感到不适，我不会站在纳粹万字旗一边。

sentences.en: I will not stand next to a swastika.
sentences.zh: 我不会站在纳粹万字旗旁边。

sentences.en: I will not stand in the same group as a swastika.
sentences.zh: 我不会和纳粹万字旗出现在同一个群体中。

sentences.en: I like adamantly refuse.
sentences.zh: 我坚决拒绝。

sentences.en: I cannot do that.
sentences.zh: 我做不到。

sentences.en: I will not stand here with any Nazi symbolism.
sentences.zh: 我不会在这里与任何纳粹象征物站在一起。

sentences.en: Like this is going to bring more violence and vitriol aimed in our direction.
sentences.zh: 这只会招致更多针对我们的暴力和谩骂。

sentences.en: We already get coffee cups thrown at us.
sentences.zh: 我们已经被人扔咖啡杯了。

sentences.en: We already get spit at and yelled at.
sentences.zh: 我们已经被人吐口水、大声辱骂了。

sentences.en: And in order to keep the people that we are inviting to these protests safe, we knew that that was not the time and place for it.
sentences.zh: 为了保护我们邀请来参加这些抗议活动的人的安全，我们知道那不是展示它的时间和地点。

sentences.en: So there's this chant,
sentences.zh: 所以有一个口号是，

sentences.en: Intifada revolution is the only solution.
sentences.zh: “起义（Intifada），革命是唯一的出路”。

sentences.en: What does that mean to you?
sentences.zh: 这对你来说意味着什么？

sentences.en: Um, so Intifada has come to represent uprising, but it means literally to shake off.
sentences.zh: 嗯，Intifada已经演变成代表“起义”，但它的字面意思是“抖落”。

sentences.en: And it is the word that has been used to label a number of violent uprisings of different Palestinian groups against Israeli occupation.
sentences.zh: 这个词被用来标记巴勒斯坦不同团体针对以色列占领的一系列暴力起义。

sentences.en: Does that seem like a fair, like actual, like official definition of it to you?
sentences.zh: 在你看来，这算是一个公平、实际且官方的定义吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I wanted to ask you if you yourself had chanted Intifada revolution in the course of the protests.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想问你自己在抗议过程中是否也喊过“起义，革命”？

sentences.en: Yeah, I have.
sentences.zh: 是的，我喊过。

sentences.en: And what did that feel like?
sentences.zh: 那是什么感觉？

sentences.en: Um, it definitely, the first time I heard it, I was uncomfortable.
sentences.zh: 嗯，第一次听到的时候，我确实感到不舒服。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Uh, whoa, this is a call for violence.
sentences.zh: 呃，哇，这是在呼吁暴力。

sentences.en: I don't like that.
sentences.zh: 我不喜欢那样。

sentences.en: But then I thought about the word.
sentences.zh: 但后来我思考了这个词。

sentences.en: I read multiple definitions.
sentences.zh: 我读了多种定义。

sentences.en: I read Jewish takes on the word.
sentences.zh: 我读了犹太人对这个词的看法。

sentences.en: I read Muslim takes on the word.
sentences.zh: 我读了穆斯林对这个词的看法。

sentences.en: I read Merriam-Webster.
sentences.zh: 我查了韦氏词典。

sentences.en: Um,
sentences.zh: 嗯，

sentences.en: And I realized the similarity in that call of there is only one solution,
sentences.zh: 我意识到“只有一种出路”这种呼吁的相似性，

sentences.en: Intifada revolution.
sentences.zh: “起义，革命”。

sentences.en: I realized the similarity to if we don't get no justice, they don't get no peace.
sentences.zh: 我意识到它与“没有正义，就没有和平”这种口号的相似性。

sentences.en: No justice, no peace.
sentences.zh: 没有正义，就没有和平。

sentences.en: When people are occupied, resistance is justified.
sentences.zh: 当人们被占领时，抵抗是正当的。

sentences.en: And yes, it is, it is, it is still a word that means these like specific actions that were taken against Israel.
sentences.zh: 是的，它仍然是一个指代针对以色列采取的特定行动的词。

sentences.en: And a lot of them harmed civilians.
sentences.zh: 其中许多行动伤害了平民。

sentences.en: And that is sad.
sentences.zh: 这很令人悲伤。

sentences.en: But it is also a word that inspires people.
sentences.zh: 但它也是一个激励人们的词。

sentences.en: It is also a word that makes people feel like they might be capable of change.
sentences.zh: 它也是一个让人们觉得他们或许有能力改变现状的词。

sentences.en: And, and yeah, I will use it thoughtfully.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我会慎重地使用它。

sentences.en: What do you mean by thoughtfully?
sentences.zh: 你所说的“慎重”是指什么？

sentences.en: In like where I time it with other chants.
sentences.zh: 比如我在喊其他口号时如何安排它的顺序。

sentences.en: Oh, what do you mean?
sentences.zh: 哦，你是什么意思？

sentences.en: I, I have like a list and they are all classified by like genre.
sentences.zh: 我有一个列表，它们都是按类型分类的。

sentences.en: So we have the financial ones and we have the, the Arabic chants and we have the chants talking about people who have died and how we are all interconnected.
sentences.zh: 我们有关于经济的，有阿拉伯语的口号，还有关于那些死去的人以及我们如何相互关联的口号。

sentences.en: And we have the chants about occupation being a crime.
sentences.zh: 我们还有关于占领是犯罪的口号。

sentences.en: And I try to put it with the no justice, no peace ones.
sentences.zh: 我试着把它和“没有正义，就没有和平”的口号放在一起。

sentences.en: Were there any other times where you felt tested by protesters?
sentences.zh: 还有其他时候你觉得受到抗议者的考验吗？

sentences.en: You felt perhaps different from them again, because of your Jewishness?
sentences.zh: 你是否因为你的犹太身份，再次感到与他们有所不同？

sentences.en: No, I feel like, I feel like there's people who feel like Zionism is Judaism, you know, or that to be Jewish, you must be ZioniSt.
sentences.zh: 不，我觉得有些人认为犹太复国主义就是犹太教，你知道，或者认为要成为犹太人就必须是犹太复国主义者。

sentences.en: But there's nothing that has come across to me as anti-Semitic if you are able to pause and remember that Israel is not Jewish people and Zionism is not Jewish people.
sentences.zh: 但如果你能停下来记住以色列不等于犹太人，犹太复国主义也不等于犹太人，那么就没有什么东西会让我觉得是反犹主义的。

sentences.en: And what about from Jewish friends?
sentences.zh: 那犹太朋友们呢？

sentences.en: Do they question what you're doing?
sentences.zh: 他们会质疑你的所作所为吗？

sentences.en: Do you ever feel some kind of people looking slightly askance at you?
sentences.zh: 你有没有感觉到有人对你侧目而视？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think, you know, my auntie made a comment once, like, if you're Jewish right now, you have to support Israel.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想，你知道，我阿姨曾经评论说，如果你现在是犹太人，你就必须支持以色列。

sentences.en: And I have definitely felt nervous about expressing some of my views in front of family.
sentences.zh: 在家人面前表达我的一些观点时，我确实感到过紧张。

sentences.en: My grandfather and I, this was a couple months ago now, we were exchanging like 1,500, 2,000 word emails, asking each other questions about our opinions.
sentences.zh: 几个月前，我和我祖父交换了大约1500到2000字的电子邮件，互相询问对方对这些问题的看法。

sentences.en: He was a history professor.
sentences.zh: 他是一位历史学教授。

sentences.en: This is my Jewish grandfather.
sentences.zh: 这是我的犹太祖父。

sentences.en: He was raised labor Zionist, but I was asking about how he was raised and the ideologies that he was raised with.
sentences.zh: 他是作为劳工犹太复国主义者长大的，但我当时在问他成长过程以及他所受的意识形态教育。

sentences.en: But he made a really good point.
sentences.zh: 但他提出了一个非常好的观点。

sentences.en: And if you have the time, I would like to try to find this line that he said and read it to you.
sentences.zh: 如果你有时间，我想试着找到他说的那句话读给你听。

sentences.en: Oh, please.
sentences.zh: 哦，请读吧。

sentences.en: Here it is.
sentences.zh: 在这里。

sentences.en: So he said, You have grown up in an era in which the deeper Israeli history is not part of your DNA.
sentences.zh: 他说：你成长的时代，更深层的以色列历史并不是你基因的一部分。

sentences.en: Jews have plenty of place in the world.
sentences.zh: 犹太人在世界上有足够多的立足之地。

sentences.en: Israel is an increasingly apartheid state.
sentences.zh: 以色列正日益成为一个种族隔离国家。

sentences.en: Most importantly, the existence of Israel has never really been under threat, nor have the most fundamental conditions of existence been an issue for Jews.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，以色列的生存从未真正受到威胁，犹太人最基本的生存条件也从未成为问题。

sentences.en: Those things are not a part of your worldview, as they are mine and my generation, and to a lesser extent, your parents.
sentences.zh: 这些事情不是你世界观的一部分，就像它们是我和我那一代人，以及在较小程度上你父母那一代人世界观的一部分一样。

sentences.en: I do not imagine you could fathom the importance of Israel in the hearts of people of my generation, nor should you.
sentences.zh: 我不认为你能理解以色列在我这一代人心中的重要性，你也不应该理解。

sentences.en: I would not ask it.
sentences.zh: 我不会要求你这样做。

sentences.en: That would be an unfair burden.
sentences.zh: 那将是一个不公平的负担。

sentences.en: That said, here are the things which I believe we might both agree on, or at the very least productively argue about.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，以下是我认为我们可能会达成一致，或者至少可以进行建设性争论的事情。

sentences.en: What did you think, really, of that point that your grandfather made?
sentences.zh: 你真的怎么看你祖父提出的那个观点？

sentences.en: Like, how did it strike you?
sentences.zh: 它对你有什么触动？

sentences.en: Did you feel like he was right, that you didn't understand why Israel would be a safe haven for people of his generation?
sentences.zh: 你是否觉得他是对的，你并不理解为什么以色列对他那一代人来说是一个避风港？

sentences.en: I think his point is that I can theoretically understand, but I cannot emotionally.
sentences.zh: 我认为他的观点是，我在理论上可以理解，但在情感上无法感同身受。

sentences.en: I theoretically understand why Israel was created, why this idea of a Jewish state was considered a good idea for the safety of Jewish people right after a genocide.
sentences.zh: 我在理论上理解为什么以色列会被建立，为什么在种族灭绝之后，建立犹太国家的想法被认为是保障犹太人安全的好主意。

sentences.en: But emotionally, like he said, I have been safe.
sentences.zh: 但在情感上，就像他说的，我一直很安全。

sentences.en: I have not been afraid for Jewish people's safety the way that I think people in other generations may have.
sentences.zh: 我并没有像我认为其他世代的人那样，为犹太人的安全感到恐惧。

sentences.en: So, that comment, I do not imagine you could fathom the importance of Israel in the hearts of people of my generation, nor should you.
sentences.zh: 所以，那句评论，“我不认为你能理解以色列在我这一代人心中的重要性，你也不应该理解。”

sentences.en: I would not ask it.
sentences.zh: “我不会要求你这样做。”

sentences.en: It would be an unfair burden.
sentences.zh: “那将是一个不公平的负担。”

sentences.en: Really, just hit my heart in a nice way, in this, like, his understanding that I will have my own perspective and he will have his own,
sentences.zh: 真的，以一种美好的方式触动了我的心，他理解我会有自己的视角，而他会有他自己的视角，

sentences.en: that lead us both towards a place of, like, understanding each other better.
sentences.zh: 这引导我们双方走向一个更好地理解彼此的地方。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Winnalou.
sentences.zh: 我是Winnalou。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games, and I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我编写《Connections》游戏，这是《纽约时报》游戏中的谜题之一，我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog, and I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗，也喜欢尝试捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Azersky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是Sam Azersky，我每天负责制作《Spelling Bee》和《Letterboxd》游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called Chromaesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做“联觉”的东西。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我在听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由像你们刚才听到的人制作的。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问nytimes.com/games，今天就开始玩吧。

sentences.en: Here's what else you should know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还应该知道的事情。

sentences.en: On Thursday, the Supreme Court rejected a challenge to the way that the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau is funded,
sentences.zh: 周四，最高法院驳回了一项针对消费者金融保护局资金筹措方式的挑战，

sentences.en: a decision that protects the agency from conservatives seeking to undermine it.
sentences.zh: 这一裁决保护了该机构免受保守派人士的削弱。

sentences.en: In a 7-2 ruling, the justices found that the way that Congress chose to finance the Bureau is constitutional.
sentences.zh: 大法官们以7比2的投票结果裁定，国会选择资助该局的方式符合宪法。

sentences.en: Had the court ruled otherwise, it may have cast doubt on every regulation and action taken by the Watchtog Agency

sentences.en: And during a second day of cross-examination, lawyers for Donald Trump sought to portray his former fixer,
sentences.zh: 在第二天的交叉质询中，唐纳德·特朗普的律师试图将他的前“调停人”迈克尔·科恩描绘成一个不断改变说辞的惯犯。

sentences.en: Michael Cohen, as a serial liar who constantly changes his story.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔·科恩，是一个不断改变说辞的惯犯。

sentences.en: Their goal was to undermine the credibility of Cohen's testimony so far, which is central to the prosecution's case in the hush money trial.
sentences.zh: 他们的目标是削弱科恩迄今为止证词的可信度，而这正是检方在封口费案中案件的核心。

sentences.en: In particular, defense lawyers seized on Cohen's claim, in a different court case, that he had lied under oath.
sentences.zh: 特别是，辩方律师抓住了科恩在另一起案件中曾承认自己在宣誓后撒谎的说法。

sentences.en: Their suggestion is that Cohen might be willing to lie under oath again during this trial.
sentences.zh: 他们的暗示是，科恩在这次审判中可能还会愿意在宣誓后撒谎。

sentences.en: This week on the show, David Marchese talks with scientist Ayanna Elizabeth Johnson about why she thinks we can't give in to climate doom, even if we feel it.

sentences.zh: 到“这到底有多严重？”
